hints.title: Strictly Lower Decreasing Jumps
hints.text: From index i, you can jump to j in range [i-d, i+d] only if arr[j] < arr[i] and all intermediate indices have arr[k] < arr[i].

hints.title: Directed Acyclic Property
hints.text: Because you can only jump to strictly lower heights, there are no cycles. The transitions form a directed acyclic graph.

hints.title: Top-Down Memoization
hints.text: Define memoized function dp(i) returning 1 + max(dp(j)) over all valid landing positions j.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unmemoized recursive search repeats sub-branches exponentially.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since transitions are strictly height-decreasing, memoization evaluates each of the N states in O(D) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate identifies DAG property and implements memoized DFS or sorts indices by height.
complexity.notes: Stopping when arr[j] >= arr[i] is essential because taller or equal pillars block further jumps.
